title: Peak angular velocity of lumbar lordosis during flexion and extension (descending/ascending), by age
condition: healthy, standing, maximal flexion and extension at preferred speed

quantity.name: lordosis angular velocity
quantity.definition: RoKs = difference between max positive and max negative lordosis-angle velocity within the exercise (Table 1); Fig 3 = mean peak velocity during descending (into max) and ascending (back to upright) movement.

source.authors: Consmuller T, Rohlmann A, Weinland D, Druschel C, Duda GN, Taylor WR
source.sample: asymptomatic volunteers aged 20-75 (no LBP in 6 months, no spinal surgery); age classes 20-35 (n=189), 36-50 (n=146), 51-75 (n=94); no BMI exclusion

protocol.summary: Self-paced lumbar flexion/extension velocities in 429 volunteers: range of functional kinematics by age (Table 1) and peak descending/ascending velocities for all volunteers (Fig 3).
how_to_use: For dynamic (time-driven) simulations of free forward bending, prescribe peak lumbar lordosis velocity ~54 deg/s going down and ~49 deg/s coming up (all ages); extension ~24 deg/s backward and ~39 deg/s returning.
Scale velocities down with age using Table 1 RoKs (flexion 114 -> 83 deg/s, extension 73 -> 47 deg/s from 20-35 to 51-75 y).
Age x sex velocities exist only in Fig 4 (not digitised).

measurement.device: Epionics SPINE strain-gauge strips 5 cm lateral of midline, lowest segment at PSIS; 50 Hz
measurement.task: 5 x maximal flexion and 5 x maximal extension at preferred speed

protocol.notes: Same Charite/Epionics volunteer database: Consmuller 2012 = all 429; Dreischarf 2014 = 323 with BMI<26; Pries 2015 = 309 (BMI<26 and valid sacral accelerometer). Do not pool these as independent samples.

extraction.uncertainty: Table exact; Fig 3 means +-1 deg/s, SDs +-1.5 deg/s (from error-bar caps; upper and lower caps agreed within 0.6)
extraction.check_notes: Fig 3 bar tops located by pixel scan (axis 0-100 calibrated to ticks, 2.81 px per deg/s) and confirmed visually on zoomed crop.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
